From 5b2c7e0ae762fff2b172caf16b2766cc3e1ad859 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Rui Salvaterra <rsalvaterra@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2021 15:30:38 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: dts: turris-omnia: fix hardware buffer management
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Hardware buffer management has never worked on the Turris Omnia, as the
required MBus window hadn't been reserved. Fix thusly.

Fixes: 018b88eee1a2 ("ARM: dts: turris-omnia: enable HW buffer management")

Signed-off-by: Rui Salvaterra <rsalvaterra@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marek Behún <kabel@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Klaus Kudielka <klaus.kudielka@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>

diff --git a/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts b/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts
index 646a06420c77..dc80a909ea88 100644
--- a/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts
+++ b/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts
@@ -32,7 +32,8 @@ soc {
 		ranges = <MBUS_ID(0xf0, 0x01) 0 0xf1000000 0x100000
 			  MBUS_ID(0x01, 0x1d) 0 0xfff00000 0x100000
 			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x19) 0 0xf1100000 0x10000
-			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000>;
+			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000
+			  MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000>;
 
 		internal-regs {
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts`**
   - A new line was added to the `ranges` property of the `soc` node. Specifically, the line:
     ```
     MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000
     ```
     was appended to the existing list of memory bus (MBus) IDs. This addition reserves the required MBus window for hardware buffer management.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in the device tree source file (`armada-385-turris-omnia.dts`) directly addresses the issue of hardware buffer management not functioning on the Turris Omnia. By reserving the necessary MBus window, the patch fixes the previously introduced bug from commit `018b88eee1a2`, which enabled hardware buffer management but did not reserve the required resources. Thus, this change is a corrective measure to ensure that the hardware buffer management can operate as intended.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: dts: turris-omnia: fix hardware buffer management
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Hardware buffer management has never worked on the Turris Omnia, as the
required MBus window hadn't been reserved. Fix thusly.

Fixes: 018b88eee1a2 ("ARM: dts: turris-omnia: enable HW buffer management")

Signed-off-by: Rui Salvaterra <rsalvaterra@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marek Behún <kabel@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Klaus Kudielka <klaus.kudielka@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of reservation for the required MBus window necessary for hardware buffer management to function correctly on the Turris Omnia. This oversight meant that even though hardware buffer management was enabled, it could not operate due to insufficient resource allocation.

 			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x19) 0 0xf1100000 0x10000
-			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000>;
+			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000
+			  MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000>;
 
 		internal-regs {

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000
MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000>;
```
Reason:
By adding the reservation for the MBus window with `MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04)`, the patch ensures that the necessary resources are allocated for hardware buffer management to function correctly on the Turris Omnia.
